audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar wilderness-itinerary and land-dispossession text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Exodus departure, forty-two-station itinerary, Aaron's death date and age, plains-of-Moab endpoint, image/high-place destruction, land allocation, and threat concerning remaining inhabitants. Strong anti-colonial, anti-genocide, and memory-ethics safeguards required.

verses.restored: These are journeys of children of Israel who went out from land of Egypt by their hosts, by hand of Moses and Aaron.

familiar.text: These are the journeys of the children of Israel, which went forth out of the land of Egypt with their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.

modern.text: These are the journeys of the Israelites when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.

original.text: אֵ֜לֶּה מַסְעֵ֣י בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצְא֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם בְּיַד מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן

verses.restored: Moses wrote their departures according to their journeys at mouth/command of YHWH; these are their journeys according to their departures.

familiar.text: And Moses wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of the LORD: and these are their journeys according to their goings out.

modern.text: At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey. These are the stages listed by their starting points:

original.text: וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת מוֹצָאֵיהֶ֛ם לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה מַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם לְמוֹצָאֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: They set out from Rameses in first month, on fifteenth day of first month. On day after Passover children of Israel went out with uplifted hand before eyes of all Egyptians,

familiar.text: And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.

modern.text: On the fifteenth day of the first month, on the day after the Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians,

original.text: וַיִּסְע֤וּ מֵֽרַעְמְסֵס֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן מִֽמָּחֳרַ֣ת הַפֶּ֗סַח יָצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: while Egyptians were burying those YHWH had struck among them, every firstborn; and upon their gods YHWH executed judgments.

familiar.text: For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the LORD had smitten among them: upon their gods also the LORD executed judgments.

modern.text: who were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them; for the LORD had executed judgment against their gods.

original.text: וּמִצְרַ֣יִם מְקַבְּרִ֗ים אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּהֶ֖ם כָּל בְּכ֑וֹר וּבֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עָשָׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁפָטִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel removed from Rameses, and pitched in Succoth.

modern.text: The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֑ס וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּסֻכֹּֽת

familiar.text: And they departed from Succoth, and pitched in Etham, which is in the edge of the wilderness.

modern.text: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר

familiar.text: And they removed from Etham, and turned again unto Pihahiroth, which is before Baalzephon: and they pitched before Migdol.

modern.text: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.

original.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵתָ֔ם וַיָּ֨שָׁב֙ עַל פִּ֣י הַחִירֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל פְּנֵ֖י בַּ֣עַל צְפ֑וֹן וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מִגְדֹּֽל

verses.restored: They set out from before Hahiroth and passed through midst of sea toward wilderness; they went a journey of three days in wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

familiar.text: And they departed from before Pihahiroth, and passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness, and went three days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham, and pitched in Marah.

modern.text: They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.

original.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַֽחִירֹ֔ת וַיַּֽעַבְר֥וּ בְתוֹךְ הַיָּ֖ם הַמִּדְבָּ֑רָה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ דֶּ֣רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר אֵתָ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּמָרָֽה

verses.restored: They set out from Marah and came to Elim; at Elim were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

familiar.text: And they removed from Marah, and came unto Elim: and in Elim were twelve fountains of water, and threescore and ten palm trees; and they pitched there.

modern.text: They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.

original.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֵילִ֑מָה וּ֠בְאֵילִם שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֞ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֛יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֥ים תְּמָרִ֖ים וַיַּחֲנוּ שָֽׁם

familiar.text: And they removed from Elim, and encamped by the Red sea.

modern.text: They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.

translation_notes: The itinerary turns movement into communal memory: departure, water, hunger, revelation, grief, and transition are mapped through place names.
Some stations and sequences differ from or supplement narrative itineraries elsewhere in Exodus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy; source and geography audit remain necessary.
Aaron's death is dated precisely and his age recorded, distinguishing his personal ending from continued priestly office.

Verses 52-56 command dispossession and destruction of Indigenous religious sites within an ancient conquest framework. They must never authorize modern colonial settlement, cultural erasure, forced conversion, ethnic cleansing, or destruction of sacred places.
The imagery of inhabitants as barbs and thorns can dehumanize populations and requires explicit restraint.
Land allocation by population and lot repeats Numbers 26 while remaining embedded in a morally contested conquest narrative.
safety_note: Never use Numbers 33 to justify colonialism, genocide, forced displacement, iconoclasm, destruction of Indigenous religion, or treating neighboring peoples as contamination. The itinerary may serve memory and accountability; the conquest commands remain ancient violence under categorical non-reenactment.
